current.text: Mark Williams is out long term with a torn labrum, which opens center minutes in Phoenix.
The Suns' starting center job is not settled. Oso Ighodaro and Maluach have both started in preseason, and their minutes are similar.
The newest projected lineup has Ighodaro starting at center and Maluach on the bench.
Experts disagree on his role. One sees him as more of a stash who will struggle to reach 24 minutes. Another says he can win the starting job on merit and would draft him over Ighodaro.
He is projected for about nine extra minutes per game, around 24 a night.
He averaged 18 points and 13 rebounds with 2 blocks and 2 threes in Summer League and was a top 10 fantasy player there.
The newest expert ranks him around 130 to 155. Experts agree he is a late flyer: do not take him inside the top 100, but round 10 is fine.
One expert sees top 75 upside if he locks in the starting job.
Phoenix has the best fantasy schedule in the league: 4, 4 and 4 games in our playoff weeks and the fewest back-to-backs.

durable.text: He profiles as a FG%, rebounds and blocks big who can add some threes.
Shot blocking is his standout skill. He converted 31.5% of rim contests into blocks, and his projected blocks are far above the top 250 pool.
He gives very few steals and assists, even for a center.
He has had some bad free throws.

note: He costs almost nothing (Yahoo average cost 1.2 USD at rank 114, ESPN 0.4 USD at rank 202, not drafted in our league), so he is a 1 to 2 USD end-of-auction pick near the 144-player cutoff. His blocks are a real outlier and he adds rebounds and FG%, so he fits punt STL and punt AST builds that need a cheap blocks source, and Phoenix's 4-4-4 playoff schedule adds late value. In the first weeks, check who starts at center and whether his minutes reach about 24. If Ighodaro keeps the job and Maluach stays near 16 minutes, he is easy to drop.
